content.en: The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, also known as the Global Goals, were adopted by all United Nations Member States in 2015 as part of the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development**. These 17 goals are integrated, recognizing that action in one area will affect outcomes in others, and that development must balance social, economic, and environmental sustainability.

definition.en: The goals apply to all nations, regardless of their development status.

definition.en: The goals are interconnected; progress in one goal often depends on progress in others.

content.en: NITI Aayog acts as the nodal institution for coordinating the implementation and monitoring of SDGs in India, including the publication of the SDG India Index.

content.en: Students often confuse the SDGs with the earlier Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). Remember that SDGs are broader in scope and apply to all countries.
